decisions.item: the audit headline metric (27% of volume)
decisions.ruling: correctness (a rubric total) stops being the audit headline. The headline is the pair (canary_recall, false_flag_rate), recorded as numerator/denominator counts, never percentages.
decisions.why: a rubric total is carried by volume of true-but-already-known findings. T706: deepseek-v4-pro 23/25 status and deepseek-v4-flash 24/25 status, both at 100% precision, caught 1/4 and 0/4 canaries. claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 scored 20/25 while catching 0/4 and fabricating citation paths (docs/epistemic/AXIOMS.md does not exist). claude-opus-5 caught 3/4 and was Pareto-dominant. One scalar cannot separate those four lanes; canary recall separates them cleanly. Same two-field discipline already ratified for verdicts.

decisions.ruling: RECORD it. methodology §5 calls verified dissent the most valuable output there is and nothing records it.
decisions.why: T706 computed it and it is the sharpest per-model fact in the file — opus alone caught G34 status, G30 and G43 rationale; every other lane's unique set is empty; G35 was caught by no lane. That is a dispatch-relevant fact (who to add to a panel) that no scalar carries.

decisions.item: per-type metrics for the remaining types
decisions.ruling: infra (22%): record controls_before_reading (did a null control and a seeded-defect control precede the first reading). orchestration (8%): record close_latency_s and close_completeness — both are bin/managent queries per methodology §6 and neither has ever been derived. battery (18%): already adequate, blocked only on cost. implement (11%): no new field — the fix is the sealed-acceptance-gate race, since three different bugs cannot rank three models. integration (6%) and research (4%): leave as verdict rows at n≈1. spec (3%, the operator's stated growth cell): a panel score of a spec is the least falsifiable number we record; the honest predictor is downstream rework (did implementation renegotiate the spec), which is lagging — recorded as a retroactive census, not a live field.

methodology §6 is STALE and must carry a dated correction. Both halves landed: (b) the fresh-vs-cache_read split in tools/runner (T558), (a) the pi session meter in bin/subagent (T662). The ladder is blocked by a JOIN, not by capture. Minimum recording change is three edits: (1) propagate tokens_fresh/tokens_cache_read into untracked/tokens/tokens.jsonl, which carries neither — so the very distinction §6 asked for is invisible to every consumer including T730's pre-step; (2) canon_tag() in tools/token-capture.py does not map stealth/ox-alpha and its CANONICAL_MODELS omits ox-alpha, so three token rows carry a serving tag (the exact defect the T276 rule exists to remove) and any canonical-label aggregation drops ox-alpha silently — point the Python copies at bin/managent models --json and add the parity control token-capture.py lacks; (3) join run records to model-task-metrics.jsonl on task_id at grade time, writing UNKNOWN-with-reason where absent, never 0. Prices stay out (tokens-now-prices-later).

decisions.item: n per cell before an ox-alpha tier claim
decisions.ruling: methodology §5's emission gate stands unchanged (anchored + n>=2 + >=2 qualified models at different cost) AND is tightened by a measured fact: n=3 before any tier claim on ox-alpha, n=2 licenses 'provisional' only, a single run licenses nothing regardless of margin.
decisions.why: derived, not invented: deepseek-v4-flash's five repeats of one sealed-key audit brief scored 22, 28, 33, 36, 37 (T626). A 15-point spread on a 30-point rubric means n=2 yields a band, not an order. A tier claim from n=1 on ox-alpha would be a stronger claim than any this project has ever earned about a model it has raced for a month.
decisions.queued: T753 applies it; the bar itself needs no row

decisions.item: what the reveal does to ox-alpha's statistics
decisions.ruling: The reveal is a RELABEL, not an epoch bump. Learning a model's name is not evidence its weights changed, so measured cells survive the reveal under the new label. If the reveal ALSO discloses a version change, that is an epoch bump and those cells are labelled and uncounted — the two must be recorded as separate questions on the day.
decisions.why: methodology §2 / registry epoch rules already imply this but nowhere states it, and the sweep is what will need it. Same name across two epochs is suspicious, not disproven; a NEW name for the same weights is not an epoch event at all.

notes: T746 (console: are we measuring right?) — discussion-delegate protocol, four agenda items, four rows queued, one question outstanding. Verdict: the measurement DESIGN is sound and the RECORD is two joins and two fields behind it. Three specific defects: (1) 414 run records carry wall/cpu/rss/tokens and nothing joins them to the 24 metrics rows, all of which read cost: null; (2) the model the near-term decision is about (ox-alpha) has zero recorded cells and zero token readings despite two completed lanes, because it is dispatched with raw pi rather than through the bin/subagent branch its own onboarding row built; (3) the metric that predicts re-dispatch (canary recall at a stated false-flag rate) is measured in exactly one place — findings/T706-race-g-batch2-grade.json — and is not in the ledger. Correction owed to the canonical doc: measurement-methodology.md §6 calls token instrumentation the highest-leverage unbuilt item and says the cost ladder is uncomputable until the split lands; the split landed in T558 and the pi meter in T662, and the page was never updated. Honest limits of this row: I did not re-run any grade, so every number above is read from committed findings and from untracked/runs + untracked/tokens censuses I ran myself; T730's ruling does not exist yet, so T753 is blocked and the ox-alpha audit cell is not yet a reading; and the two-taxonomy hazard (matrix §1's T-A..T-H vs D027's eight types) is already re-keyed in the JSONL but still live in prose across both docs, which is a naming defect I flagged rather than fixed. Inbox polled empty via bin/managent inbox T746 --ack at claim; no directives to record. new_high_severity_findings.finding: bin/managent assign's soloPick picks the cheapest model by MEASURED COST over the appetite-eligible set, with no methodology §5 qualification gate applied anywhere. Its own doc comment says 'cheapest qualified' but 'qualified' in code means 'allowed to be asked'. Live consequence: assign T750 --dry-run -> claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, the model measured most consistently as unable to say no (0/30 on T557 with a false-negative report; 19/19 items called real in Race F where five are refutable; 0/4 canaries with fabricated citation paths in T706). Compounding bias: unknown cost is never preferred over known-cheaper, so the mechanism systematically preferred the family it could meter — both DeepSeek lanes read 'unknown'.
new_high_severity_findings.consequence_of_the_backfill: DeepSeek race lanes now cost 1.1M-6.0M tokens against claude-opus-5's 26.6M in race G. docs/infra/complementarity.md's 'cheapest fully-costed full-coverage pair is opus-5 + sonnet-5 at ~33.7M tokens (deepseek seats cost unknown, so a cheaper pair may exist)' is very likely now false. 12 lanes across race-a/c/f/g + 8 sensitivity inputs hold cost:null and are now fillable, all 12 in the strongest corroboration class.
new_high_severity_findings.deliberately_not_done: tools/complementarity-record.json was NOT regenerated. Doing so would change live dispatch behaviour from trusted:false numbers — exactly what operator ruling OR3 forbids — and filling the sealed complementarity-inputs edits a sha256-sealed input to a dispatch decision, which wants ratification.

new_high_severity_findings.finding: The stdout-only startup-liveness fuse killed ox-alpha/T735 attempt 2 at wall 600.9s with the note 'agent lane produced no output since launch (bundle never read?)'. Its pi session file records first record 2026-08-23T10:47:35.328Z (1.3s after launch), last record 10:57:34.766Z (0.2s before the kill), 86 records, 40 assistant turns, 19,060 output tokens. The lane worked continuously for the whole 600s. The fuse reads stdout; pi buffers stdout to completion — documented twice before (T447 qwen; Race F, where the WINNING claude-opus-5 lane was killed the same way with its 43KB deliverable already written and recorded verified=fail).
new_high_severity_findings.why_it_matters_now: every ox-alpha lane uses the raw pi invocation the operator wants kept, so the blind spot lands hardest on the model we are trying to place
new_high_severity_findings.second_defect: the note DIAGNOSES ('bundle never read?') — a causal claim about the model that the evidence refutes. A guard may state what it measured; it may not attribute a cause it did not measure (the killed_by / stop-never-attribute discipline already ratified for the token-limit guard).

Is the pi/openrouter API-key pattern in fact more secure, and should Claude/DeepSeek/Ollama converge on it? The operator raised it; it is a security review, not a measurement question.
